title_en: Yixing Jiangong Construction and Installation Co., Ltd. v. Zhang Xin and Zhang Xueshan — dispute over liability for damages from application for property preservation during litigation
ruling_gist_en: Due to the varying levels of legal knowledge, ability to adduce evidence to prove the facts of the case, and capacity to analyze and determine legal relationships among the parties, they generally cannot meet the professional standards required for judicial adjudication. Therefore, a party's judgment on the facts in dispute and his rights and obligations may not necessarily be consistent with the judgment of the people's court. The standard of the duty of care required of a party applying for preservation should not be overly strict. If the sole criterion for determining whether an application for preservation is erroneous is whether the applicant's claims are supported by the judgment, this would inevitably hinder a bona fide party from protecting his rights through the litigation preservation procedure as allowed by law, and would affect the functioning of the litigation preservation system. Moreover, Article 6 and Article 7 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China provide that tort liability is based on the principle of fault liability, and that no-fault liability must have a statutory basis. However, the no-fault liability provided for in the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China does not include the liability for damages caused by an erroneous application for preservation. Therefore, for an erroneous application for preservation, it must be established that the applicant was subjectively at fault; it cannot be sufficient to find error merely because the applicant's claims were not upheld.

full_text_en:
Yixing City Construction and Installation Co., Ltd. v. Zhang Xin and Zhang Xueshan — dispute over liability for damages arising from application for property preservation during litigation

【Ruling Summary】

Because the parties differ in their legal knowledge, ability to adduce evidence of the facts of the case, and ability to analyze and determine legal relationships, they generally do not meet the professional standards required for judicial adjudication. Therefore, a party's assessment of the facts in dispute and its rights and obligations may not necessarily be consistent with the court's judgment. The duty of care required of a party applying for preservation should not be overly stringent. If the sole basis for determining whether an application for preservation is erroneous were whether the applicant's claims were upheld, it would inevitably hinder bona fide parties from lawfully protecting their rights through the litigation preservation procedure, and impair the function of the litigation preservation system. Moreover, Articles 6 and 7 of the Tort Law of the People's Republic of China provide that tort liability is based on the principle of fault liability, and that no-fault liability must have a legal basis. However, the no-fault liability provided for in the Tort Law of the People's Republic of China does not include liability for damages arising from erroneous application for preservation. Therefore, an erroneous application for preservation requires the applicant's subjective fault as a constituent element, and it cannot be deemed sufficient merely because the applicant's claims were not upheld.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court
(2018) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 2027

Re-applicant (plaintiff at first instance, appellant at second instance): Yixing City Construction and Installation Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 6, Chaquan Road, Yixing Environmental Science and Technology Park, Yixing City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal representative: Zhang Yayi, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Fei Jianxin, attorney at Jiangsu Tongyun Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Qiang, attorney at Jiangsu Tongyun Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance, appellee at second instance): Zhang Xin, female, born on May 26, 1987, Han Chinese, domiciled at Room 201, Unit 3, Building 9, No. 246 Shanda Road, Lixia District, Jinan City, Shandong Province.

Respondent (defendant at first instance, appellee at second instance): Zhang Xueshan, male, born on August 30, 1964, Han Chinese, domiciled at No. 62 Qingnian Street, Xinzhuang Village, Huanglou Subdistrict Office, Qingzhou City, Shandong Province.

The re-applicant Yixing City Construction and Installation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yixing Construction Company), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2017) Lu Min Zhong No. 1932 (hereinafter referred to as the second-instance judgment) rendered by the Shandong High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Shandong High Court) in the case concerning the dispute over liability for damages arising from an application for property preservation during litigation between it and the respondents Zhang Xin and Zhang Xueshan, applied to this court for retrial. This court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to conduct the review, which has now been concluded.

Yixing Construction Company applied for retrial on the following grounds: The basic facts found in the second-instance judgment lacked evidentiary support. 1. There is no judicial interpretation defining "error" within the meaning of Article 105 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. However, the error in Zhang Xin's application for property preservation could not only be inferred from the outcome of the loss of the lawsuit, but could also be confirmed from the litigation where Zhang Xin fabricated facts. 2. The second-instance judgment's finding that Zhang Xin had no malice in applying for litigation preservation lacked evidentiary support. Yixing Construction Company was not a party to the "Loan Contract" involved in the case and should not have been named as a defendant. The testimony of the witness Zhang Xinyou at trial was entirely based on Zhang Xin's statements. The cash journal of the Qingzhou City Urban Exhibition Hall Project submitted by Zhang Xin was false and insufficient to prove the actions of Yixing Construction Company. Yixing Construction Company had not issued any power of attorney. The power of attorney submitted by Zhang Xin to the court was false and could not be used as a basis for finding Yixing Construction Company liable for repayment. In other private lending dispute cases, Zhang Xin chose to sue only Weng Xiaogang and withdrew the lawsuit against Yixing Construction Company, which demonstrated that she knew the evidentiary materials were false. Because Zhang Xin fabricated accounts, provided false evidence, misappropriated the power of attorney, and knowing the error still applied for litigation preservation, her application for litigation preservation should be found to be malicious. 3. The second-instance judgment's finding that Zhang Xin's application for litigation preservation did not cause actual loss to Yixing Construction Company lacked evidentiary support. Zhang Xin applied to freeze Yixing Construction Company's bank accounts, which prevented Yixing Construction Company from normal operations and forced it to borrow from non-financial institutions and other entities and individuals, with borrowing interest rates several times higher than bank loan interest rates. By the time the accounts were unfrozen, Yixing Construction Company had already paid interest of up to RMB 10,698,900. This loss should be borne by Zhang Xin and the guarantor Zhang Xueshan. Therefore, the application for retrial was filed pursuant to Article 200(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Zhang Xin and Zhang Xueshan submitted written opinions stating that an erroneous application for preservation should be premised on the applicant's intentional or gross negligence, and the outcome of the litigation should not be the sole criterion for determining whether the application for preservation was erroneous. Zhang Xin had no malice in applying for litigation preservation, was not at fault, and objectively caused no loss to Yixing Construction Company. Yixing Construction Company had a relationship with the third parties Yixing Antai Construction and Commercial Housing Development Co., Ltd. and Jiangsu Wenzhuo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. This case was a fictitious lawsuit fabricated through malicious collusion among the three companies.

Upon review, this court finds: Based on the grounds for retrial submitted by Yixing Construction Company and the evidence submitted, the issues in dispute in this case are: (1) whether an erroneous application for preservation can be deemed sufficient solely because the applicant's claims were not upheld; (2) whether the second-instance judgment's finding that Zhang Xin had no malice in applying for litigation preservation lacked evidentiary support; and (3) whether the second-instance judgment's finding that Zhang Xin's application for litigation preservation did not cause actual loss to Yixing Construction Company lacked evidentiary support.

I. Issue 1: Whether an erroneous application for preservation can be deemed sufficient solely because the applicant's claims were not upheld.

Article 105 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If an application is erroneous, the applicant shall compensate the respondent for losses suffered as a result of the preservation." Because the parties differ in their legal knowledge, ability to adduce evidence of the facts of the case, and ability to analyze and determine legal relationships, they generally do not meet the professional standards required for judicial adjudication. Therefore, a party's assessment of the facts in dispute and its rights and obligations may not necessarily be consistent with the court's judgment. The duty of care required of a party applying for preservation should not be overly stringent. If the sole basis for determining whether an application for preservation is erroneous were whether the applicant's claims were upheld, it would inevitably hinder bona fide parties from lawfully protecting their rights through the litigation preservation procedure, and impair the function of the litigation preservation system. Moreover, Articles 6 and 7 of the Tort Law of the People's Republic of China provide that tort liability is based on the principle of fault liability, and that no-fault liability must have a legal basis. However, the no-fault liability provided for in the Tort Law of the People's Republic of China does not include liability for damages arising from erroneous application for preservation. In summary, an erroneous application for preservation requires the applicant's subjective fault as a constituent element, and it cannot be deemed sufficient merely because the applicant's claims were not upheld.

II. Issue 2: Whether the second-instance judgment's finding that Zhang Xin had no malice in applying for litigation preservation lacked evidentiary support.

Yixing Construction Company argued in its retrial application that Zhang Xin's actions in the other case, including fabricating accounts, providing false evidence, and misappropriating the power of attorney, demonstrated her subjective malice. However, these assertions were merely suspicions of Yixing Construction Company, and it did not submit sufficient and effective evidence to prove them. This court does not support this argument. Some of the "Receipts for Payments" issued by the third party Weng Xiaogang to Zhang Xin bore the official seal of the Qingzhou City Urban Exhibition Hall Project Department of Yixing Construction Company. Zhang Xin provided a power of attorney issued by Yixing Construction Company, claiming that Weng Xiaogang was the manager of the Qingzhou Project Department of Yixing Construction Company and was responsible for fundraising, project planning, and construction of the relevant project of Yixing Construction Company. Yixing Construction Company also acknowledged in the first-instance of this case that Weng Xiaogang was operating under its name. Based on these facts, Zhang Xin named Yixing Construction Company as a defendant and, to ensure smooth enforcement of the future effective judgment, applied to seal the bank account deposits of Yixing Construction Company within the scope of the subject matter in dispute. This was an exercise of the litigation rights conferred by law. Zhang Xin's choice in other private lending dispute cases to sue only Weng Xiaogang and withdraw the lawsuit against Yixing Construction Company was also an exercise of litigation rights to protect her substantive rights in accordance with the law. From this, it cannot be inferred that she had the subjective malice to harm Yixing Construction Company's rights by applying for litigation preservation. Therefore, Yixing Construction Company's ground for retrial that the second-instance judgment's finding that Zhang Xin had no malice in applying for litigation preservation lacked evidentiary support cannot be sustained.

III. Issue 3: Whether the second-instance judgment's finding that Zhang Xin's application for litigation preservation did not cause actual loss to Yixing Construction Company lacked evidentiary support.

In the first-instance, Yixing Construction Company submitted evidence such as a power of attorney, a loan agreement, a construction contract for a construction project, receipts for withdrawals and remittances, and receipts for interest payments to prove that Zhang Xin's application for litigation preservation caused it interest losses. However, the official seal on the power of attorney was clearly inconsistent with the seal on the complaint in this case, and neither of the two loan contracts was entered into in the name of Yixing Construction Company, nor were the subsequent interest payments made through the company. Furthermore, according to Yixing Construction Company's own statements, it was the judgment debtor in hundreds of enforcement cases, and it was impossible to determine whether the losses were caused solely by Zhang Xin's application for litigation preservation. Yixing Construction Company did not submit sufficient and effective evidence to prove the interest losses it claimed, nor did it prove a causal relationship between the losses suffered and Zhang Xin's application for litigation preservation. Therefore, Yixing Construction Company's ground for retrial that the second-instance judgment's finding that Zhang Xin's application for litigation preservation did not cause actual loss to it lacked evidentiary support also cannot be sustained.

In summary, Yixing Construction Company's application for retrial does not meet the circumstances provided in Article 200(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 204(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 395(2) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court rules as follows:

The application for retrial by Yixing City Construction and Installation Co., Ltd. is dismissed.

Presiding Judge: Cheng Xinwen
Judge: Liu Yinchun
Judge: Fu Shaojun
June 25, 2018
Clerk: Wu Zelong
